# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 22 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 22 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_022_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 4, Chapter 1

**1** The fourth vision I saw, brothers and sisters, came twenty days after the previous one. It was a foreshadowing of the coming tribulation. **2** I was walking on the country road — about ten stades from the main road — through difficult terrain. **3** As I walked alone, I was asking the Lord to complete all the revelations and visions he had been showing me through his holy church, to strengthen me and grant repentance to those servants of his who had stumbled, so that his great and glorious name might be glorified — for he had thought me worthy to show me his wonders. **4** While I was praising and thanking him, something like a responsive voice came to me: "Do not be double-minded, Hermas." I thought to myself, "How could I be double-minded? The Lord has established me and I have seen such glorious things." **5** Walking a little further, brothers and sisters — I saw dust rising up toward the heavens and thought, "Are cattle approaching?" It was about a stade away from me. **6** As the dust rose higher and higher I suspected something supernatural was near. A little light broke through, and I saw a great beast like a massive sea-monster, from whose mouth fiery locusts were issuing. It was about a hundred feet in length, and its head was like an earthenware pot. **7** I began to weep and beg the Lord to rescue me. Then I recalled what I had heard: "Do not be double-minded, Hermas." **8** So — clothed in faith in the Lord and calling to mind the great things he had taught me — I took courage and turned to face the beast. It was charging with such force and speed that it could have flattened a whole city. **9** When I drew near, the great beast stretched out on the ground and did nothing except extend its tongue; it lay completely still until I had passed. **10** The beast had four colors on its head: black; then fiery and blood-red; then golden yellow; then white.

---

*LOGOS note: Vision 4 is the apocalyptic centerpiece of the Visions. Passing the beast by faith alone is the central dramatic event. The four colors will be allegorically interpreted in ch. 23.*
